finding: NeverD Decoder exposes its Capstone handle through public getHandle(). Public cs_option calls can mutate text/detail/syntax/mnemonics independently of Decoder::setText/setDetail. A sealed-options or initialization-only fast entry cannot be introduced by assuming the handle is immutable.
implication: Current dispatch prototypes retain all option and callback checks. Future prepared-context work must handle public mutation boundaries and reused handles explicitly, and compare actual NeverD behavior before changing consumer entry points.
prior_cache_scope: R1183 already updated public-option eligibility at mutation boundaries while keeping callbacks, doing_mem and global vsnprintf checks live. Repeating initialization caching alone would not address its recorded performance losses.
qualification: This is an ownership constraint for future designs, not a new confirmed public API bug or a request to change the current dispatch prototypes.
